where: Lead, Section 2 heading/content, and Figure caption
problem: The chapter calls all four responses 'first-order'. A band-pass or band-stop built from a high-pass plus a low-pass (or a twin-T) has two reactive sections, so it is second-order, not first-order. A single first-order section cannot produce a peak or a notch. The plotted band-pass/band-stop curves (peak 1 and zero at x = 1) are second-order shapes, so the label contradicts the figure itself.
fix: Say: 'Two first-order responses, low-pass and high-pass, plus two second-order responses, band-pass and band-stop, which are built by combining the first-order sections.' Change the figure caption to 'the four basic responses' and note in Section 2 that the band-pass and band-stop are second-order.

problem: The plotted band-pass |H| = 1/√(1+(x−1/x)²) and band-stop have Q = 1. The cascade described in the text, when the two sections are set to the same cut-off (f_L = f_H), gives Q = 1/3 and a peak of only 0.5 at f0 before normalising. A student who computes the cascade and compares it with the figure will think the calculation is wrong.
fix: Add one line: 'The band-pass and band-stop curves in the figure are drawn for Q = 1. For a cascade of two first-order sections with f_L = f_H, Q = 1/3, so the peak at f0 is only 0.5 before normalising; separating f_L and f_H raises Q.'
